what is a joule | what does a joule measure | what is the joule unit => The joule (J) is the SI unit of energy and work. It's named after James Prescott Joule, an English physicist who studied heat. Lifting a small apple 1 meter takes about 1 joule.

what is a lux | what does a lux measure | what is the lux unit => The lux (lx) is the SI unit of how much light falls on a surface. Bright sunlight is about 100,000 lux, and a well-lit office about 500 lux.

what is a degree celsius | celsius vs kelvin | how do you convert celsius to kelvin => A degree Celsius is the same size as a kelvin, but the scales start in different places. Add 273.15 to a Celsius temperature to get kelvin, so 0 °C is 273.15 K.
celsius to fahrenheit formula | c to f => Multiply by 9, divide by 5, then add 32. So 20 °C is 68 °F, and 100 °C is 212 °F.
when are celsius and fahrenheit the same | what temperature is the same in c and f | minus 40 degrees => Minus 40 is the same in both: minus 40 °C equals minus 40 °F.
what is a liter | how big is a liter => A liter is a unit of volume equal to 1,000 cubic centimeters, a cube 10 cm on each side. One liter of water has a mass of about 1 kilogram.
what is a milliliter | ml vs cm3 => A milliliter is a thousandth of a liter, exactly the same as one cubic centimeter. A teaspoon holds about 5 mL.
what is a tonne | metric ton | how much is a tonne => A tonne, or metric ton, is 1,000 kilograms. A small car has a mass of roughly one tonne.
what is an atmosphere unit | atm pressure unit | how many pascals in an atmosphere => One standard atmosphere (atm) is 101,325 pascals, about the air pressure at sea level.
what is a bar pressure unit | millibar | hectopascal => A bar is 100,000 pascals, close to air pressure at sea level. Weather maps use millibars or hectopascals, which are the same size: 1,013 mb is typical.
what is psi | pounds per square inch | tire pressure units => PSI means pounds per square inch, a pressure unit used in the US for tires and air tanks. Air pressure at sea level is about 14.7 psi.
what is a newton meter | what is torque measured in | unit of torque => Torque, a turning force, is measured in newton meters (N m): a force of one newton acting one meter from the pivot.
what is a kilowatt | how much is a megawatt | kilowatt vs megawatt => A kilowatt is 1,000 watts and a megawatt is a million watts. A microwave uses about 1 kilowatt, and a big wind turbine can produce a few megawatts.
what is a gigawatt | how much power is a gigawatt | 1.21 gigawatts => A gigawatt is a billion watts, about the output of a large nuclear power station.
what is a nanosecond | how long is a millisecond | microsecond meaning => A millisecond is a thousandth of a second, a microsecond a millionth, and a nanosecond a billionth. Light travels about 30 cm in a nanosecond.
what is a micrometer unit | how small is a micron | micron meaning => A micrometer, or micron, is a millionth of a meter. A human hair is about 50 to 100 micrometers thick.
what is an angstrom | angstrom unit | how small is an angstrom => An ångström is a ten-billionth of a meter (0.1 nanometers). Atoms are about 1 to 3 ångströms across, so it's handy in chemistry.
what is a decibel scale | how loud is 100 decibels | decibel examples => Decibels measure loudness on a scale where every 10 dB is 10 times more intense. Whispers are about 30 dB, talking 60 dB, a rock concert 110 dB. Long exposure above about 85 dB can damage hearing.
what is a calorie vs a kilocalorie | food calories vs calories | what is a kcal => A food Calorie is actually a kilocalorie, 1,000 small calories, which is about 4,184 joules. It's enough energy to warm 1 kg of water by 1 °C.
what is a knot speed | how fast is a knot | why do ships use knots => A knot is one nautical mile per hour, about 1.85 km/h. Ships and planes use it because a nautical mile is tied to Earth's latitude, which helps navigation.
what is a nautical mile | nautical mile vs mile | how long is a nautical mile => A nautical mile is exactly 1,852 meters, a bit longer than a regular mile (1,609 meters).
what is a hectare | how big is a hectare | hectare vs acre => A hectare is 10,000 square meters, a square 100 m on each side, about 2.5 acres. A soccer field is roughly 0.7 hectares.
what is a dalton | atomic mass unit | what is amu => A dalton, or atomic mass unit, is one twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom, about the mass of a proton or neutron. Atomic masses on the periodic table are in daltons.
